item.title: Signs of danger at Iowa ammunition plant emerged months before Army says it knew, emails show
item.description: Contractors at the facility in Middletown, Iowa, where the government plans to detonate several tons of degrading lead explosives on Wednesday, sought to neutralize the hazardous material nearly six months before the Army says it became aware the munitions posed a risk, documents reviewed by The Washington Post show. Operators’ request to a Georgia-based explosives disposal company on Sept. 24, 2025, asked for a plan to “neutralize and dispose” of 68 drums of lead azide at the plant.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego García will leave U.S. voluntarily to avoid deportation, ending 20-month legal saga
item.description: The Salvadoran migrant living in Maryland was illegally deported to his home country, then brought back to the U.S. and threatened with deportation to African countries.

item.title: House Democrat vows to investigate Trump’s efforts to reshape Smithsonian after photos of apparent overhaul plan surfaced
item.description: Rep. Chellie Pingree of Maine and the Smithsonian’s outgoing secretary, Lonnie G. Bunch III, defended the institution’s independence a day after news broke of purported plans that include firing more than a dozen employees.

item.title: Trump awards the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani, a longtime friend and former personal lawyer
item.description: Giuliani, a former mayor of New York, became the face of President Donald Trump’s unsuccessful efforts to overturn the results of his 2020 reelection loss. It’s uncommon, although not unprecedented, for a president to give the award to a prominent political ally.

item.title: Democrat flips a Tennessee House district, AP reports, adding to the record majority her party will have in January
item.description: Victoria Broderick has won the U.S. House seat in Tennessee’s 4th Congressional District, according to the Associated Press, giving Democrats 259 seats in the lower chamber — a modern record.

item.title: Army says it must detonate lead azide to avoid a ‘worst-case scenario’ and urges Iowa town’s vulnerable residents to evacuate
item.description: The controlled detonation of the highly sensitive explosive compound set for Wednesday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown is needed, federal officials said, because the lead azide has become increasingly unstable and is at risk to explode on its own.
